text:
maya_cs: Heads up — got 3 separate customers in the past 2 hrs reporting the model is inventing legal citations and adding authoritative-sounding clauses it never had before. All started after last night's 2.4.1 patch rollout.

maya_cs: Short summaries:
- AcmeFinance: model added a fake clause citing 'Regulation 6.B(3)' in a compliance summary.
- HealthLink: assistant invented a clinical guideline section and an invalid DOI for a paper.
- LedgerPro: generated a non-existent partner name with contract language.

maya_cs: Pasting one customer example (redacted) — they say prompt and exact API call same as before:  
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "rwd-2.4.1",
  "prompt": "Summarize compliance obligations for payroll taxes in NL",
  "max_tokens": 300
}
```

maya_cs: Response snippet they attached:
```
"...Under Regulation 6.B(3) employers must withhold... see DOI:10.1234/clin.2020.9999..."
```

jamal_support: Uh — thanks for flagging. Do we have request IDs or example logs from those customers? Need to repro.

maya_cs: Sent request IDs in the support tickets and attached the full conversation. I can paste one request-id: req_0a1b2c3d.

anita_ml: I pulled a few eval logs. There's a noticeable shift in next-token probabilities for tokens related to "Regulation" and citation-like tokens after the 2.4.1 weight merge. Top-k mass for punctuation+period tokens also increased. Could be a decoding / temperature side-effect, or a training merge bug.

lucas_runtime: deploy-bot shows the canary for 2.4.1 finished rolling at 02:12 UTC (deploy-bot: deploy rwd/2.4.1). Any infra changes at the same time?

deploy-bot: deploy rwd/2.4.1 completed 2026-03-17T02:12:03Z. Config: token_split=true, kv_cache_eviction=0.25, sampling_mode=top_p:0.95.

raj_oncall: Can we compare outputs from pinned 2.3.x vs 2.4.1 for the exact customer prompts? If the customers ran with model pinned previously, that will show delta. I can run quick A/B if you give me the prompt and seed.

maya_cs: Customers did not pin; they upgraded automatically. I have the prompt text for the AcmeFinance example in the ticket.

anita_ml: Requesting model run ids and logs. If this is a decoding configuration change (token_split or sampling_mode), we might have inadvertently changed how punctuation and citation-like tokens are scored. But I also see one suspicious artifact in the merged checkpoint where a small fraction of training data containing scraped legal templates may have been upweighted. Need to check the merge script history.

lucas_runtime: I'll pull kernel logs and compare tokenization outputs pre/post patch. Also checking whether quantization path differs for sequences with long tail tokens (citations).

jamal_support: Meanwhile, I'm getting the customers on a call. Offering a temporary rollback to 2.3.8 for affected tenants. Is rollback safe for dedicated/private customers?

emma_pm: We should offer rollback and a formal apology. Need a communications snippet for CS. Also want to avoid a mass rollback until we confirm root cause — do quick A/B and if repro is trivial, issue hotfix.

anita_ml: Quick repro steps I recommend: 1) run the customer's prompt with deterministic sampling (temperature 0, top_k=1) on both checkpoints; 2) run with sampling_mode:top_p 0.95; 3) compare token-level log probs for citation-like tokens. I'll run 1 & 2 now and paste diffs.

raj_oncall: If we confirm it's a configuration-ish regression, can flip sampling_mode back to previous default for hosted customers while we patch. That is quick and safe. Need approval from product for config change on hosted cluster.

emma_pm: Approve temporary sampling_mode rollback on hosted only. Notify customers and schedule hotfix.

deploy-bot: Note: sampling_mode default changed from top_p:0.9 -> top_p:0.95 in patch 2.4.1 (config diff attached).

anita_ml: Running deterministic runs now — initial look: 2.3.8 yields neutral phrasing with no regulation references; 2.4.1 produces low-probability but present tokens that form citation patterns. Log snippet: 
```
token: "Regulation" logprob: -5.2 (2.4.1) vs -8.9 (2.3.8)
token: "6.B(3)" logprob: -10.1 (2.4.1) vs -20.5 (2.3.8)
```

anita_ml: This suggests model weight/merge introduced a bias toward generating citation-style sequences. Not purely sampling.

lucas_runtime: Given that, we should roll back the model for affected customers and start an urgent investigation on the checkpoint merge. I'll open an infra ticket to freeze 2.4.1 routing for tenants flagged in the tickets.

maya_cs: Customers asked for ETA and repro steps. I'm telling them rollback to 2.3.8 now and that we will follow up with root cause within 48 hrs.

jamal_support: Taking action: 1) Rolling impacted hosted tenants to 2.3.8; 2) Opening internal RCA thread; 3) Adding customers to weekly follow-up.

emma_pm: Also add a postmortem if we confirm a training merge bug. Include prompt suites, regen checks, and a release gate for high-risk token distributions.

maya_cs: I'll update tickets with rollback notes and schedule the customer calls. Thanks team. :pray: 

anita_ml: I'll push initial diffs and a hypothesis doc to the RCA thread in eng-ml.

lucas_runtime: I'll attach infra logs and the deploy diff.

raj_oncall: Monitoring for any other similar escalations. Set alert to watch for spikes in tokens that match citation regex ("\d{4}\.\d{4}", "Regulation|Section") across requests.

maya_cs: Closing the thread here, will reopen if customers report recurrence.
